lines.text: Starting today, you see exactly ten seconds ahead.
Not a feeling. Not a hunch.
A ghost version of the world, playing ten seconds early.
You can't pause it. You can't turn it off.
And it never, ever skips.
That's the whole power. Let's see how far ten seconds can take you.
Day one. Your alarm hasn't rung yet, but you already know it will.
You reach for your coffee, and see the mug slide off the counter.
So you catch it, before it falls.
No more stubbed toes. No more spilled milk. No more missed buses.
Out on the street, a skateboard shoots from nowhere. You're already three steps to the side.
You're officially the luckiest person alive.
And you haven't even tried yet.
Now, let's get competitive.
Table tennis. Your opponent smashes the ball, and you've already seen where it lands.
Boxing. A punch takes less than half a second. You watched it ten seconds ago.
Every fighter in the world moves like they're underwater.
A fastball flies at your face at ninety miles an hour. You tilt your head, slightly. Bored.
Nobody can beat you at anything that happens in the next ten seconds.
And that's almost everything.
But ten seconds isn't only for games. Sometimes it's for running.
A thief grabs a bag and bolts through the crowd. You don't chase him. You step in front of where he's about to be.
Cars on the road? You see every one of them, before the driver does.
You cross six lanes of traffic at a walk. Horns screaming. Not one of them touches you.
Then a bus, a bike, a pigeon, a man with a ladder. Every obstacle shows up as a ghost, a whole breath before it arrives.
It looks like talent. It looks like magic. To everyone watching, you're just impossibly smooth.
You are not fast. You are early.
And being early is better than being fast.
So you turn it into money.
Roulette. The ball spins, and you see where it lands, before the dealer does.
The casino bans you in an hour.
So you try the stock market.
Prices flicker, and you see every tick before it happens.
For a trading computer, ten seconds is an eternity. For you, it's a printing press.
A thousand dollars. A million. A billion.
And you never leave your apartment.
Money buys a lot. But it can't buy this.
It's a normal Tuesday. A city of ten million people, going to work.
And in the ghost world, the ground begins to break.
Ten seconds before the first tremor, you see the cracks, the falling glass, the buildings swaying.
Here's a real fact. Earthquake warning systems give people about ten seconds. And ten seconds is enough to save thousands of lives.
Trains slow down. Surgeons pull their hands away. Elevators stop at the nearest floor.
But you don't have a siren. You have a voice, and ten seconds, and a street full of strangers who don't believe you.
So you scream. You point. You run. And one by one, they run with you.
The city shakes. Dust fills the sky. And when it clears, most of them are standing.
Ten seconds. That's all it took.
Then, one evening, the ghost world shows you something awful.
A child's ball rolls into the road. A truck, ten seconds away, can't stop.
You run. You have ten seconds, and you know every one of them.
You grab her. The truck roars past, inches behind you.
She never even knows how close it was.
But the ghost world doesn't choose what it shows you.
It shows you everything. Even what you can't reach in time.
Here's the problem nobody warns you about.
You're never surprised again.
Your friend tells a joke. You've already heard it. You laugh ten seconds early.
A surprise party. You see everyone hiding. You pretend to be shocked.
Every conversation plays twice. Every song. Every goodbye.
Slowly, the world stops feeling real. It feels like a rerun.
Ten seconds becomes a hall of mirrors, and you're the only one inside.
Then you notice something strange. What you see, depends on what you do.
So you run a test. Simple. You decide to raise your left hand, but only if the ghost raises its right.
The ghost raises its left hand. You raise your right. The ghost changes.
Which means the ghost isn't the future. It's a guess. A guess about what you'll do after seeing the guess.
A snake eating its own tail, ten seconds long.
And there's one thing it can never show you. The moment you finally decide to ignore it.
So you close your eyes. And for the first time in months, you don't know what happens next.
It's terrifying. And it's the best feeling you've had all year.
Because the future was never the gift. The surprise was.
Weeks pass. You've saved lives, you've made millions, and you've learned to love surprises again.
Then one morning, the ghost world goes quiet.
The street is empty. The sky is black. Just you, standing still.
Not ten seconds of future. Ten seconds of nothing.
The ghost doesn't blink. It doesn't move. It just waits.
Which means ten seconds from now, something ends.
What would you do with ten seconds?
Tell me in the comments.
